notes: A second, independent review of public NDL scans. An unqualified timetable row is not treated as daily service. OCR was used only to locate candidate text; every reported timetable or legend statement was checked against the cited scan canvas.

research_queue.notes: NDL PID 914814 was reviewed across all 37 OCR pages and the relevant original canvases. R0000008 gives the special-express rows; R0000009 says a Tokyo-Shimonoseki special express is in operation. Other pages use explicit limited-operation annotations (for example the seasonal date range on R0000007 and symbol/date annotations on R0000017), but no affirmative daily, weekday, or enumerated-date rule was found for trains 1 or 3. Absence of an annotation is not calendar evidence. Next evidence target: a Railway Ministry working timetable, official operating notice, or issue legend that expressly assigns operating days to trains 1 and 3.

NDL PID 1212739 canvas R0000002 is explicitly titled 東京下関間主要列車時刻表, so it cannot prove that every passenger stop is shown. Canvas R0000122 lists the limited-express names, endpoints, train numbers/classes, and origin departure times as of the 1934-12-01 revision. Canvas R0000127 has a scoped sleeper-list note that ※ trains run only when passenger demand is high; it does not state that every unmarked limited express runs daily. Acquire the original December 1934 Railway Ministry/Japan Tourist Bureau timetable or an official working timetable/notice with complete calls and operating-day rules.

Resolve only against existing rail-history identities that are valid on 1934-12-01. Do not map historical station names to current N02 identities by name alone. This candidate does not upgrade route-line completeness.

source_documents.notes: The content hash is for the NDL IIIF manifest bytes fetched on the access date. This is a contemporary commercial handbook digitized by NDL, not a Railway Ministry publication. Canvas R0000002 contains the principal-train table; R0000122 defines the limited-express services; R0000127 contains the demand-only symbol note scoped to a sleeper-equipped-train list. Official NDL OCR was used for discovery and checked against the scans. No scan is committed.

evidence_review.finding: The down principal-train table directly shows trains 3 and 1 as special expresses between Tokyo and Shimonoseki, with the endpoint times already recorded in reviewed-historical-batch.
The passenger-rule page says that a special express operates between Shimonoseki and Tokyo, but gives no recurrence or operating-day rule.
evidence_review.locator: NDL PID 914814, IIIF canvas R0000009, printed pp. 4-5

evidence_review.finding: The issue contains explicit limited-operation annotations for other trains, including a seasonal date range and symbol/date notes. Those annotations do not apply to the special-express rows and do not define an all-unmarked-trains-are-daily default.
evidence_review.locator: NDL PID 914814, IIIF canvases R0000007 and R0000017

timetable_candidates.why_not_canonical: No explicit operating calendar was found for trains 1 or 3. The existing historical station-reference gap also remains.

timetable_candidates.page_or_locator: NDL PID 1212739: R0000002 (東京下関間主要列車時刻表); R0000122, printed pp. 222-223 (special-express definitions); R0000127, printed pp. 232-233 (scoped demand-only symbol note)
timetable_candidates.why_not_canonical: The table is expressly limited to principal trains/stations and does not establish complete passenger calls. Neither the table nor the service-definition page states a daily, weekday, or enumerated-date operating calendar. The demand-only symbol note is scoped to a different sleeper-equipment list, so an unmarked row cannot be promoted as daily.
